```{python}
#| label: setup
# Connection: PGHOST / PGPORT / PGUSER / PGPASSWORD / PGDATABASE environment variables
# (defaults: localhost, 5432, postgres, no password, parcel_qa). The Python results are read from
# PARCELQA_PY_SUMMARY (default ../out/qa_summary.csv, the file parcel_qa.py writes).
import os, csv, datetime
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.engine import URL

eng = create_engine(URL.create(
    "postgresql+psycopg2",
    username=os.environ.get("PGUSER", "postgres"), password=os.environ.get("PGPASSWORD"),
    host=os.environ.get("PGHOST", "localhost"), port=int(os.environ.get("PGPORT", 5432)),
    database=os.environ.get("PGDATABASE", "parcel_qa")))
q = lambda sql: pd.read_sql(sql, eng)

summary = q("SELECT * FROM qa.summary ORDER BY check_code")
py_path = os.environ.get("PARCELQA_PY_SUMMARY", "../out/qa_summary.csv")
py = {r["check"]: int(r["count"]) for r in csv.DictReader(open(py_path))} if os.path.exists(py_path) else None
totals = q("""SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM core.parcels) AS parcels,
                     (SELECT count(*) FROM qa.active_addresses) AS addresses,
                     (SELECT count(*) FROM core.road_centerlines) AS roads,
                     (SELECT count(*) FROM qa.findings) AS findings,
                     (SELECT postgis_lib_version()) AS postgis,
                     (SELECT split_part(version(), ' ', 2)) AS pg""").iloc[0]

FOREST, OLIVE, INK2, RULE = "#2e4a34", "#6d7a3a", "#4c5a4f", "#c7ccbb"
SEV = {"high": "#d03b3b", "medium": "#ec835a", "low": "#fab219"}
plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": ["Public Sans", "Segoe UI", "DejaVu Sans"], "font.size": 9,
                     "axes.edgecolor": RULE, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "xtick.color": INK2, "ytick.color": INK2})

def md_table(df, align=None, widths=None):
    """pandas -> Markdown table without extra packages (renders in HTML and PDF); widths in percent."""
    cols = list(df.columns)
    align = align or ["l"] * len(cols)
    sep = ["---:" if a == "r" else ":---" for a in align]
    rows = ["| " + " | ".join(cols) + " |", "| " + " | ".join(sep) + " |"]
    for _, r in df.iterrows():
        rows.append("| " + " | ".join(str(v).replace("|", "/") for v in r.values) + " |")
    if widths:
        rows.append("")
        rows.append(': {tbl-colwidths="[' + ",".join(map(str, widths)) + ']"}')
    return Markdown("\n".join(rows))

fmt = lambda n: f"{int(n):,}"
```

## Summary

```{python}
#| output: asis
match = py is not None and all(py.get(c, 0) == n for c, n in zip(summary.check_code, summary["count"]))
print(f"""The toolkit checks **{fmt(totals.parcels)} tax parcels**, **{fmt(totals.addresses)} active address points** and
**{fmt(totals.roads)} road centerline segments** from Sheboygan County's public GIS services for 19 kinds of error
that matter to land records and NG911 call routing. It found **{fmt(totals.findings)} items to review**.

The same 19 checks are written twice: once in Python (GeoPandas) and once as spatial SQL views in PostgreSQL
{totals.pg} with PostGIS {totals.postgis}. """ + (
 f"On this run the two versions agree on every check: **{fmt(sum(py.values()))} findings in Python, "
 f"{fmt(totals.findings)} in SQL**." if match else
 ("The table below compares the two versions check by check." if py else
  "The Python results file was not found, so this run shows the SQL results only.")))
```

## Results by check

```{python}
t = summary.copy()
t["Check"] = t.check_code
t["What it finds"] = t.title
t["Severity"] = t.severity
t["SQL"] = t["count"].map(fmt)
cols = ["Check", "What it finds", "Severity", "SQL"]
align = ["l", "l", "l", "r"]
if py is not None:
    t["Python"] = t.check_code.map(lambda c: fmt(py.get(c, 0)))
    t["Match"] = ["yes" if py.get(c, 0) == n else "**no**" for c, n in zip(t.check_code, t["count"])]
    cols += ["Python", "Match"]; align += ["r", "l"]
t["Per 1,000"] = t.rate_per_1000.map(lambda v: f"{v:.2f}")
cols += ["Per 1,000"]; align += ["r"]
widths = [8, 38, 12, 10, 10, 9, 13] if py is not None else [10, 50, 14, 12, 14]
display(md_table(t[cols], align, widths))
```

Rates are per 1,000 features of the layer the check looks at (parcels, address points or road segments).
Checks with zero findings are kept in the table: a clean result is a result.

## Where the findings are

```{python}
#| label: fig-map
#| fig-cap: "Every finding, colored by severity. Municipal boundaries in gray."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 8.4
f = gpd.read_postgis("SELECT severity, geom FROM qa.findings", eng, geom_col="geom")
m = gpd.read_postgis("SELECT label, geom FROM core.municipalities", eng, geom_col="geom")
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
m.plot(ax=ax, facecolor="#e6e9dd", edgecolor="#9aa38c", linewidth=0.5)
for sev in ["low", "medium", "high"]:          # high drawn last, on top
    s = f[f.severity == sev]
    s.plot(ax=ax, color=SEV[sev], markersize=9, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4,
           label=f"{sev.title()} ({len(s):,})", zorder=3)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 1.0), frameon=False, title="Severity", alignment="left")
ax.set_axis_off(); ax.set_aspect("equal")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Findings cluster where addresses and small parcels are dense: the City of Sheboygan, Plymouth, Sheboygan Falls
and the villages. Rural strings of findings usually follow one road segment whose address range is wrong, which
shows up as a run of "number outside road range" findings.

```{python}
#| label: fig-muni
#| fig-cap: "Municipalities with the most address and road findings per 1,000 address points (at least 500 address points)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.6
r = q("""
WITH a AS (SELECT m.label, count(*) AS addresses
           FROM qa.active_addresses p JOIN core.municipalities m ON ST_Within(p.geom, m.geom) GROUP BY m.label),
     f AS (SELECT m.label, count(*) AS findings
           FROM qa.findings x JOIN core.municipalities m ON ST_Within(x.geom, m.geom)
           WHERE x.layer IN ('addresses', 'roads') GROUP BY m.label)
SELECT a.label, a.addresses, coalesce(f.findings, 0) AS findings,
       round(coalesce(f.findings, 0) * 1000.0 / a.addresses, 1) AS per_1000
FROM a LEFT JOIN f USING (label) WHERE a.addresses >= 500
ORDER BY per_1000 DESC LIMIT 10""")
r = r.iloc[::-1]
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
bars = ax.barh(r.label, r.per_1000, color=FOREST, height=0.62)
for b, v, n in zip(bars, r.per_1000, r.findings):
    ax.text(b.get_width() + 0.3, b.get_y() + b.get_height() / 2, f"{v:.1f}  ({n} findings)", va="center", color=INK2, fontsize=8)
ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0); ax.set_xlabel("Findings per 1,000 address points")
ax.grid(axis="x", color="#e1e0d9", linewidth=0.6); ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.set_xlim(0, r.per_1000.max() * 1.35)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Per address, two rural towns stand out. In the Town of Lyndon, 39 address points sit outside their road
segment's number range and 28 sit unusually far from the segment they are linked to: a handful of segments with
wrong ranges or wrong links flag whole strings of rural addresses. The Town of Lima shows the same pattern on a
smaller scale.

## One example of each

```{python}
ex = q("""SELECT DISTINCT ON (check_code) check_code AS "Check", title AS "Finding", feature_id AS "Feature", detail AS "Detail"
          FROM qa.findings ORDER BY check_code, feature_id""")
display(md_table(ex, widths=[8, 24, 22, 46]))
```

Every finding has a point on the map and a sentence that says what to look at. Three patterns explain most of them:

- **Number outside road range** (the largest group) usually means the road segment's range is too short, or the
  point is linked to the wrong segment. When a nearby segment of the same street does fit the number, the detail
  says so.
- **Gaps and overlaps between parcels** are a few square meters each: digitizing slivers where neighboring
  parcels were drawn at different times.
- **Missing attributes** are mostly parcels without an owner or municipality that are not road right-of-way.

## How the database is built

```{python}
s = q("""SELECT table_schema AS "Schema", table_name AS "Table" FROM information_schema.tables
          WHERE table_schema IN ('core', 'lkp') AND table_type = 'BASE TABLE' ORDER BY table_schema, table_name""")
s["Rows"] = [fmt(q(f'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM {a}.{b}').n[0]) for a, b in zip(s.Schema, s.Table)]
display(md_table(s, ["l", "l", "r"], [20, 50, 30]))
```

- **`src`** holds the four layers exactly as downloaded, reprojected to Wisconsin Transverse Mercator (EPSG:3071,
  meters) so distance and area thresholds match the Python version.
- **`lkp`** holds lookup tables, the database version of geodatabase domains: address status, road class and
  status (which roads are expected to carry address ranges), municipality types, the check list and the thresholds.
- **`core`** holds typed, constrained copies: primary keys, foreign keys to the lookups, CHECK constraints on
  address ranges, typed geometry columns, a repaired geometry next to the original, generated columns for
  normalized street names, and GiST spatial indexes.
- **`qa`** holds one materialized view per check, all with the same four columns (`check_code, feature_id,
  detail, geom`), plus `qa.findings` (every finding as one point layer, used by ArcGIS Pro) and `qa.summary`.

## How to rerun

```text
activate arcgispro-py3-qa
cd ParcelQA_postgis
REM download the layers, load them into PostGIS, run the SQL checks
python postgis\load_postgis.py config\sheboygan.json
REM run the Python checks on the same files
python parcel_qa.py config\sheboygan.json out
REM build this report (HTML and PDF)
set PGPASSWORD=<postgres password>
quarto render report\parcel_qa_report.qmd
```

When the county updates its data, these steps rebuild every number, table and map in this report.
